dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Kevin, how can I help you this morning?

Good morning, sir. Thank you for answering. I know City Hall is closed today, it is Sunday, so I am sorry to call this line, but I did not know where else, and I am, um, a little worried about my house.
No, you're in the right spot, that's what this line's for on the weekend. What's going on?
My name is Wilson Lopes. We live at 3 Wellington Avenue, in the Fifth Ward. With the storm, the one Friday into Saturday, our basement took water. Overnight, Friday night going to Saturday.
Okay. Wilson Lopes... L-O-P-E-S?
Yes, exactly, L-O-P-E-S.
Got it. Three Wellington Avenue. Writing that down. Basement water overnight Friday into Saturday, the tenth. How much water are we talking?
About three inches, sir. Three inches on the floor. It came in by the back cellar door and also by the basement windows, the small ones low on the wall.
Back cellar door... and the basement windows. Okay. And is this groundwater, you think, or is it coming off the street?

From the street, I am sure of it. I was looking out the window Friday night, because the rain was very heavy, and the drain at the corner, the street drain, the water was coming up out of it. Like a fountain, almost. It came up from the drain first, and then it went across and into the yard and then into the house. [line breaks up] ...so I think the drain is the problem.
Sorry, you cut out for a sec there. The drain was coming up and then what?
Excuse me. I said the water came out of the drain first, and after that it came to the house. The drain, it was not taking the water. It was giving it back.

Yeah, okay, that's a backup. So, catch basin at the corner backing up into the street, then into the property. I'm putting that down as a drain backup at the corner by 3 Wellington. Did you see anything on the grate, like leaves, sand, anything piled on it?
It was dark, I could not see well. Yesterday morning there was a lot of sand and some leaves around it, yes. I did not touch it. I did not know if I am permitted.
That's alright. What about inside, did anything get damaged down there?

Yes, this is my worry. We have boxes with the kids' school things, papers, old notebooks, the things you keep, you know. Those got wet at the bottom. And a spare refrigerator we keep down there, the water was around it. I unplugged it, but I am afraid to plug it again. I do not know if it is safe. Also the basement is finished, there is carpet in part of it, and I am worried about the smell, the mold.
Yeah, I'd hold off on that fridge till it's good and dry, honestly, maybe have somebody look at it. Okay. Wet boxes, spare refrigerator. Is the water out now?
Mostly, yes. We used the wet vacuum all day yesterday. But they say more rain this week, and if the drain is the same, it will happen again, no? This is what I am afraid of.

Understood. So here's what I can do. I'm logging it as a drain backup and I'll get a crew out to check that corner tomorrow, Monday. They'll look at the grate and the basin and clean out whatever's in there.
Tomorrow. Thank you, sir, very much. Do I need to be home for them?
Nope, it's all out in the street, they don't need to come in. Can I grab a phone number for the work order, though?
Of course. It is 401-555-0132. This is a cell phone.

And one more question, if you permit me. The boxes, the refrigerator. Is there a form, a claim, for damage? Because the water came from the city drain. I do not want to make problems, I only want to know if this exists.

Sure, fair question. There is a claim process, it goes through the City Clerk's office, not us. They're closed today, obviously, but you can call them tomorrow or stop in and ask for the claim form. Take pictures of everything now, the boxes, the fridge, the water line on the wall if there is one.
Pictures, yes. My husband took some yesterday, I will take more. [inaudible] the receipts also?
Sorry, receipts? Yeah, if you have them, hang onto anything you've got.
Okay. Okay. The City Clerk, tomorrow. I will write it.
I'm writing too, we're both busy over here.

[pause] Yes. Actually I have a pen in my hand already, I was doing the crossword this morning to calm my nerves a little. In pen, always, my husband says this is arrogant. And I am stuck on one clue for an hour. Seven letters, "heavy downpour." Can you believe it?
That's a little on the nose for this weekend. Seven letters... cloudburst's too long. Deluge's six.
Six, yes, I tried. Never mind, it will come. I should not keep you, you have other calls with this storm.

It's been a busy one. Okay, so just to read it back: Wilson Lopes, 3 Wellington Avenue, drain at the corner backed up overnight Friday into Saturday, about three inches in the basement through the back cellar door and the windows, wet boxes and a spare fridge. Crew checks the corner Monday. Claim form through the City Clerk.
Yes, all correct. And if it rains before tomorrow, and the water comes again, I call this number?
Yep, call right back here. Somebody's on it all day.
Thank you, Kevin. I am still nervous, I will be honest, but it helps to know somebody comes. Have a good Sunday, sir.
You too, Mr. Lopes. Hope it stays dry over there.
